data.title: Regex
data.tagline: A notation for describing text to match, search, or constrain
data.learningOutcome: Given a common regex, you can say what it accepts and rejects, and judge whether it is sufficient.
data.description: A regular expression describes text patterns for matching, searching, or constraining an input, such as \d for digits and + for one or more. This page uses JavaScript regex syntax to constrain a numeric-text field; a match only means the text fits this rule, not that a phone number or email is valid.

learning.assumes: You have seen form validation messages, or regexes in AI replies.
learning.outcome: Given a common regex, you can say what it accepts and rejects, and judge whether it is sufficient.

distinctions.label: Wildcard
distinctions.explanation: Filename wildcards often use * and ? to stand for a string or one character; that is a different rule system from regex. A regex can describe structures such as digits followed by an @.

distinctions.label: Validation rule
distinctions.explanation: A business validation rule is a judgment like must agree to terms; a regex only matches text patterns and knows nothing about business meaning.

explanation.title: Common symbol meanings
explanation.text: In this example, \d is one digit and + means one or more; ^ and $ mark the pattern's boundaries; brackets can list allowed characters.

explanation.title: Test it with real inputs
explanation.text: To judge whether a regex fits, test both matching and non-matching boundary inputs, such as digits, symbols, and empty values.

explanation.title: Acceptance must cover rejects
explanation.text: Testing only passing cases is not acceptance; confirm results for inputs that should be rejected, including spaces, letters, and empty values.

data.boundary: This example uses JavaScript regex syntax; other languages and tools can differ. A match only means the text fits this pattern, not that a phone number, email, or other business value is valid.

lessonPractice.title: AI uses /^\d+$/ to constrain a text field. What does this regex accept?

options.label: One or more digits only; letters and symbols do not match
options.feedback: Correct. \d is a digit and + means one or more; this checks digit-only text, not its business meaning.

options.label: A match means this is a valid phone number
options.feedback: It only checks whether the text contains digits; phone validity depends on the region and business rules.

options.label: Any text at all
options.feedback: The leading ^ and trailing $ require the input to fit the whole pattern, not arbitrary text.

data.agentPrompt: Use /^\d+$/ to constrain a numeric-text field. Test digits, letters, spaces, and empty input; confirm the pass and reject results match the rule. Do not present it as phone-number validation.
